bib.title: A Comparative Study on Reasoning Patterns of OpenAI's o1 Model

legacy_report:
SOURCE: A Comparative Study on Reasoning Patterns of OpenAI's o1 Model. Siwei Wu, Zhongyuan Peng, Xinrun Du, Tuney Zheng et al. (M-A-P, OpenO1 Team); arXiv:2410.13639v2, 22 Oct 2024; labelled "Preprint".
COVERAGE: 14 of 14 pages; 43,647 of 43,647 chars read (body, results, case studies, conclusion). References skimmed only. No appendices with results exist. Neither note nor references.md currently cites 2410.13639 (grep found no match).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- o1 beats GPT-4o test-time-compute baselines on most benchmarks, most clearly on math and code.
  number: overall 34.32 (o1-preview), 35.77 (o1-mini), 24.70 (Agent Workflow), 18.44 (GPT-4o). USACO: o1-preview 44.60, o1-mini 12.23, GPT-4o 5.04. AIME: o1-preview 44.00, o1-mini 62.00, GPT-4o 12.22.
  setup: four filtered benchmarks (HotpotQA 274, Collie 226, USACO bronze 139, AIME 90 problems from 2022-24). Baselines use GPT-4o as backbone. Single reported run, no variance.
  quote: "the OpenAI's o1 model achieves the best performance on most benchmarks compared to previous Test-time Compute methods and GPT-4o, particularly in Math and Code tasks."
  where: p.4-5, Table 1
- More reasoning does not always help. o1-mini beats o1-preview on AIME and Collie but loses on USACO.
  number: Collie 53.53 (mini) vs 34.07 (preview); AIME 62.00 vs 44.00; USACO 12.23 vs 44.60.
  setup: as above.
  quote: "the o1-mini surpasses the o1-preview on some tasks, it shows that the reasoning process of o1 does not always lead to better improvements."
  where: p.5
- On Collie (strict format constraints), o1 re-states the constraints in its reasoning (Emphasizing Constraints) and keeps reasoning short. The authors say this stops long reasoning from breaking the format.
  number: none (qualitative, from 20-30 hand-labelled samples per benchmark)
  quote: "This allows the model to place greater emphasis on Collie's output format requirements, preventing the generation of an excessively long reasoning process that would result in outputs not meeting the format requirement."
  where: p.6, Fig 10 case study
- Six o1 reasoning patterns: Systematic Analysis, Method Reuse, Divide and Conquer, Self-Refinement, Context Identification, Emphasizing Constraints. Which one dominates depends on the task.
  number: counts only in Fig 1/2 (not in the text). Samples: 20-30 per benchmark.
  quote: "for commonsense reasoning tasks, o1 tends to use CI and EC. In contrast, in math and coding tasks, o1 mainly relies on MR and DC."
  where: p.2 and p.5-6
  caveat: the text is inconsistent about the top patterns. The intro says "DC and SR"; p.5 says "SA and DC appear most frequently" and then says "SR and DC play a crucial role". The "key to o1's success" claim is a guess ("might be").
- Agent Workflow (GPT-4o with domain-specific system prompts) closes much of the gap to o1. Step-wise BoN and Self-Refine do not.
  number: Agent Workflow USACO 22.22 vs GPT-4o 5.04; Collie 46.07 vs 43.36; AIME 15.56 vs 12.22. Step-wise BoN N=4: Collie 19.55, AIME 7.78. Self-Refine Collie 0.00.
  setup: Agent Workflow uses a published agent framework for HotpotQA and Collie, and custom GPTs (code copilot, math solver) for USACO and AIME.
  quote: "it designs a series of domain-specific system prompts, which reduces unnecessary long-context reasoning processes."
  where: p.5
  caveat: the "due to the system prompt" attribution is an assumption (they write "we assume"). No ablation of the prompt.
- o1's reasoning-token length varies by task, not by input length or correctness.
  number: Fig 3 only (bar chart, roughly under 1000 tokens). No exact values in the text. The 273.59 / 450.31 / 439.90 / 262.51 in Table 2 are Step-wise BoN intermediate-step tokens, not o1.
  quote: "the number of reasoning tokens for correct and incorrect samples is similar for the same task, and there is no clear correlation between the input prompt length and the length of the reasoning tokens."
  where: p.7, Fig 3
  caveat: the reasoning tokens are the summarized thought text, extracted by a rule.
- BoN is capped by the reward model and the search space. Human-chosen answers raise HotpotQA accuracy; N beyond 8 stabilises or declines.
  number: other reward models under 15% on HotpotQA vs 33% with a human reward model (N=4).
  quote: "their accuracies are under 15%), while the human-based reward model could help to improve the LLMs' ACC to 33%."
  where: p.7-8, Fig 4, Fig 5
  quote2: "When N > 8, the performance of the models either stabilizes or declines"
- BoN and Step-wise BoN can hurt on format-strict tasks.
  number: Collie GPT-4o 43.36, BoN N=4 39.82, N=8 38.50; Step-wise BoN N=1 5.31. Step-wise BoN gain on HotpotQA at N=4: 2.55 points.
  quote: "Step-wise BoN achieves less than 12% accuracy on Collie, and its performance on AIME is only half that of other methods"
  where: p.6
  note: the quoted "less than 12%" is the text's claim; Table 1 shows 19.55 for N=4 (N=1 is 5.31). The text and the table disagree.
- o1-preview results fluctuate between AIME years, and o1-mini stays near 60%.
  number: o1-preview best 57% on AIME24, around 40% on AIME22/23; o1-mini "around 60%".
  quote: "in o1-preview, the best performance on AIME24 is 57%, while results on the other two datasets are both around 40%."
  where: p.9-10, Fig 6

LIMITS
- Only o1-preview, o1-mini and "o1-web" were tested. Comparing o1 with GPT-4o methods mixes model-capability differences with the method, so it is not a controlled test of "what o1 does".
- The pattern counts come from 20-30 hand-labelled samples per benchmark. The paper gives no inter-annotator agreement and does not say who labelled them.
- It gives no confidence intervals or repeated runs.
- The datasets were filtered to samples that other LLMs (Llama3-72B, Qwen-72B, Claude, and others) fail on. This shifts absolute numbers and makes them non-comparable to the standard benchmarks. The text names slightly different model lists in different places.
- The "reasoning tokens" are the summarised thinking shown by the API, not raw chains.
- The causal claims (domain prompts explain Agent Workflow's win; DC and SR are "the key to o1's success") are stated as assumptions.
- The GPT-4o reward model is both weak and the same family as the generator.
- The Table 1 "Overall" column mixes benchmarks of different scale, so treat it as a rough summary only.
- Dated: 2024 models (o1-preview, GPT-4o). Nothing on the effort setting, system prompts for reasoning models, or prompting reasoning models directly.
- Relevance to note 07: weak. The paper does not test prompt wording on reasoning models. Its usable points are that reasoning patterns vary by task, that constraint restatement appears in o1's thoughts, and that more or longer reasoning is not always better. It does not support "state goals, not steps" directly.

BUILDS ON: Best-of-N and Step-wise BoN (reward-model search); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2024); Snell et al. (2024) on scaling test-time compute; the agent framework of Zhou et al. (2023, 2024); LIME (Zhu et al., 2024) for data filtering; benchmarks HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018), Collie (Yao et al., 2023), USACO (Shi et al., 2024), AIME (AI-MO validation set); reward models Skywork-Reward-Gemma-2-27B (Liu & Zeng, 2024), URM-LLaMa-3.1-8B (Lou et al., 2024), RewardBench (Lambert et al., 2024).

CODE: none in the paper. Code and data repo: https://github.com/Open-Source-O1/o1_Reasoning_Patterns_Study

FIGURES (the extraction gave captions and text; I did not run the figures script)
- Fig 1/2 (p.6): reasoning-pattern frequency per benchmark and overall (SA, MR, DC, SR, CI, EC; y-axis to about 80). It shows which patterns dominate each task faster than prose does.
- Fig 3 (p.7): o1 reasoning tokens per task (all, correct, incorrect, input). It shows that correct and incorrect lengths are similar.
- Fig 4 and Fig 5 (p.8): BoN by reward model, and by N from 1 to 16.
- Fig 10 (p.11): the Collie case, where o1 restates "be/of/is" constraints in its thinking. It is the best illustration for note 07.
- Table 1 (p.4): the full results grid.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. The extraction is mostly clean, but Figs 1-6 appear as axis text only, so bar values are unreadable. AIME math in Fig 9 is garbled. The text says "less than 12%" Step-wise BoN on Collie but Table 1 gives 19.55 at N=4. The pattern-ranking statements are internally inconsistent, as noted above.
